title: [D4 Contract] Versioned agent request/result contract with typed failure envelope
summary: `helena/contracts/` is the second versioned package: `__init__.py` holds the loader and its two exceptions, `v1.py` holds the frozen `AgentRequest` / `AgentResult` / `AgentFailure` triple plus the closed vocabularies they validate against, and `check_exchange` holds the four rules that live between a request and its outcome. The three fields `concept/04` refuses are absent, forbidden by `extra="forbid"`, and asserted absent by name over every model and over the module's AST.
assumption_validated: That one typed request/result pair can carry both agents without a free-text channel, and that the concept's asymmetries can be enforced by the shape rather than by review. Result: positive for all but two. Enforced structurally -- the citation rule and its two exemptions, `unknown`'s mandatory gaps, the closed root set per emitter (through `helena.taxonomy.for_emission`), triage having no tool budget and no retrieval trace / evidence package / proposed claim / tool cost, a budget-exhausted run never returning `normal`, a typed failure with nowhere to put a verdict, the echoed versions, a citation resolving only to evidence the run was given, and a truncated rendering forcing a `truncated` gap on the outcome. NOT enforceable here and named as other increments': `concept/04`'s "triage sees evidence tier `enrichment` only" (the rendering carries no tier -- the renderer's rule, D4 Rendering) and budget enforcement itself (`concept/07` puts it at the tool boundary). One negative result worth recording: the request cannot carry a `VersionSet`, because `model_version` is the identity the *response* reported and a request has no response yet.
makes_buildable: The renderer (task 27-29) has the shape it must produce: `Rendering` with the five closed section names, `RenderedSection.evidence_ids` and `Truncation`. The model client and triage runner (30-31) have the object to validate structured output into, the bounded-retry exit (`AgentFailure(reason="schema_invalid")`), and `RequestVersions.completed_by(reported_model)` for recording what actually answered. The policy increments (32-33) have `Citation`, `Gap` and the per-emitter root check to sit beside. D5 storage has the typed columns and the `(assessment, evidence, role)` join row payload.

verification.detail: 877 passed in 375.58 s (the whole suite, engine tests included), of which 99 are the new tests/test_contracts.py. No SQL was added, so nothing new was executed against an engine; the contract is Pydantic classes and a pairing function and needs none. Two mutations were run to check the tests bite rather than describe: disabling the truncation-visibility rule in `check_exchange` failed exactly one test, and adding a `task: str = ""` field to `AgentRequest` failed two -- the by-name test and the AST test. `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` and `uv lock --check` both clean; no dependency was added.

escalations.detail: Four fields exist that concept/04's own list of request/result contents does not name, each recorded in docs/decisions/0017-the-agent-contract.md rather than slipped in. (1) `sensor` on the request -- helena.context.FrozenContext is keyed by (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version), so 'the context reference and its version, which is what makes replay possible' does not resolve without it. (2) `emitter` on the request AND on the result -- the closed root set and the tool rules are per agent, and a stored result has to be validatable on its own, which is what replay does. (3) `RequestVersions` instead of a `VersionSet` on the request, plus an optional `model_version` on the failure -- ADR-0008 makes `model_version` the identity the response reported, and a request has no response; a `model_unavailable` failure has none either, and recording the configured name there would be exactly the substitution the registry exists to prevent. (4) `RenderedSection.evidence_ids` -- concept/04 requires every enriched value to be citable, and listing the identifiers is what makes 'a citation resolves to something the run was given' checkable instead of aspirational. Reviewable and revertible in a v2; none of them widens what an agent may do.

Two readings of concept/02 that could have gone the other way, both recorded in ADR-0017. (a) `EvidencePackage` holds `patterns` and `narrative` only. concept/02 lists four parts -- 'indicators, patterns, missing information, narrative' -- and concept/04 separately lists the citations and the gaps as result fields; the indicators ARE the citations and the missing information IS the gaps, so carrying them inside the package too would be two copies of one fact that can disagree. (b) The `normal` citation exemption is triage's alone: concept/04 says 'a `normal` **triage** decision returns verdict and confidence only', so an analyst `normal` requires a citation. That is deliberate rather than an oversight -- concept/02's composition rule says '`normal` on contacted indicators never establishes `normal` for the context on its own', and an uncited analyst `normal` would be the one verdict in the system with nothing behind it.

deferred: No structure inside `RenderedSection.body`. The five section NAMES are the contract's; what goes in one belongs to `rendering_version`, and the renderer is task 28. Deciding a body shape here would be building the rendering before anything had been measured about how large one is -- and v1 is frozen, so task 28 must not need to edit it. That is exactly why the rendering is held at a versioned boundary rather than inlined.

No size budget on the rendering. concept/08 lists the numeric budget values as open and concept/07 makes budget values 'policy, not constants in a branch'. `Truncation` guarantees that dropping something is recorded; how much may be dropped is task 29's.

No check of cost against budgets. Enforcement is at the tool boundary (concept/07); a run that overshot its wall clock by a hair would otherwise become a contract error rather than the typed failure it is.
No monetary cost field. concept/06 makes monetary cost derived, and no price table exists in this repository -- a currency column filled from a guessed rate would be an invented external fact.

No disclosure record. concept/02 and concept/07 put it on the assessment and it is decided at the provider-tool boundary; `RetrievalStep`'s cache-hit-versus-live-query is what one will be derived from.

No assessment table, no sink message, no citation join rows. concept/03 describes all three; they belong to the increment that first stores an assessment. So the typed failure is typed but NOT yet stored or counted -- concept/instruction.md §7's 'every new failure path is typed, stored and countable' is satisfied for the enrichment layer and stays open for the agent layer until D5.
Triage's 'evidence tier `enrichment` only' is not enforced by the contract, because the rendering carries no tier. It is the renderer's rule and task 28 lists it.
lessons: task 26: A REQUEST CANNOT CARRY A `VersionSet`. `helena.versions.VersionSet.model_version` is the identity the model's RESPONSE reported (ADR-0008), and a request is written before any response exists. So `RequestVersions` holds the eight dimensions known in advance plus `model_requested`, and `completed_by(model_version)` mints the nine-dimension set once something has answered. The same problem bites the failure envelope harder: a `model_unavailable` failure is a run where NOTHING answered, so it records no model version at all -- `AgentFailure` therefore carries `RequestVersions` plus an optional `model_version`, required for `schema_invalid` and forbidden for `model_unavailable`.

task 26: THE `normal` CITATION EXEMPTION IS TRIAGE'S ALONE. concept/04's sentence is 'a `normal` **triage** decision returns verdict and confidence only', and the natural misreading -- every `normal` is exempt -- was caught only because a test builder defaulted to an analyst `normal` and the model refused it. concept/02's composition rule is the reason it should refuse: '`normal` on contacted indicators never establishes `normal` for the context on its own'.

task 26: A VERSION MODULE THAT MUST STAY FROZEN CANNOT HOLD THE THING THE NEXT TASK WILL BUILD. `contracts/v1.py` is frozen the moment a row records `schema_version = "v1"`, so the rendering had to be held at a boundary the renderer can fill without editing v1: five closed section names, a per-section evidence-id list, a truncation record, and a `body` this contract does not look inside. Any richer rendering shape here would have forced task 28 to edit a frozen module.

task 26: THE CONSTANTS A VERSION VALIDATES AGAINST BELONG IN THE VERSION MODULE, NOT IN THE PACKAGE. Triggers, section names, stances, gap kinds, retrieval outcomes and failure reasons all live in `v1.py`: a constant in `contracts/__init__.py` is one every frozen version imports, so editing it would edit `v1` through the same side door `tests/test_package_layout.py` refuses a shared helper for. Three shapes still come from outside and are frozen BY REFERENCE -- `VersionSet`, `helena.taxonomy` and `QueryFailure` -- and that hazard is recorded in ADR-0017 rather than designed away, because the alternative is four vocabularies re-spelled in every future contract version.

task 26: `check_exchange` EXISTS BECAUSE THREE RULES BELONG TO NEITHER OBJECT. The emitter matching, the eight version dimensions coming back unchanged (which is what concept/04's word 'echoed' means), and a citation resolving only to an evidence id the rendering showed or the retrieval trace produced. A fourth is about visibility rather than pairing: a rendering that truncated something forces a `truncated` gap on the outcome, because 'truncation is visible or it is a bug' has to hold in the RECORD of the run and not only in the input to it.

task 26: A FIELD ABSENT BY CONVENTION COMES BACK, SO IT IS REFUSED THREE WAYS. No such field; `extra="forbid"` on every model; and a test asserting the absence by name over every model AND over the module's AST -- the AST arm is what catches a field added to a model the test file forgot to list. Mutation-checked: adding `task: str = ""` to `AgentRequest` fails both arms.

task 26: BUDGET EXHAUSTION IS NOT A FAILURE REASON. concept/07 requires a budget-exhausted run to return a verdict on what it gathered, degraded to `unknown` and never `normal`. So it is a `Gap` kind, `AgentResult` refuses `normal` beside it, and `FAILURE_REASONS` is the three ways a run produced no verdict at all: `schema_invalid`, `model_unavailable`, `timed_out`.
task 26: The full suite is now 877 tests in ~376 s on this machine (99 of them the new contract tests), up from the 593 in ~157 s task 17 recorded. Budget a session against the larger number.
failed_approaches: task 26: Putting the contract classes in `helena/agents.py` beside the runners was considered and rejected before it was written. ADR-0008 retains agent output schemas as frozen Pydantic classes; a class inside `agents.py` would be edited every time the runner around it changed, and `tests/test_package_layout.py` already has the machinery that makes a versioned package's freeze structural. `agents.py` stays the deferred runner placeholder and its docstring now points at `helena.contracts`.

task 26: Storing the classification `root` as a field beside the path. Rejected for the reason `helena.enrichment.EnrichmentEvidence.verdict` gives: the taxonomy already refuses a path whose root is not its first segment, so a stored root is a second copy of a fact that cannot disagree in the model and can in a table. The task step names 'root, classification path'; the root is a derived property and a test asserts there is no field.

task 26: Carrying the assessment's identity (tenant, sensor, context reference, host, window) on `AgentResult` as well as on `AgentRequest`. Rejected: it is the request's, the pair is what gets stored and emitted, and concept/03's sink message is assembled from the context and the assessment together. Consequence the next session should know: an `AgentResult` or `AgentFailure` alone does not say which context it is about -- `check_exchange(request, outcome)` is the pairing, and D5 writes the row from both.
next_session_should_know: `helena.contracts.version("v1")` returns a `ContractVersion` with `.request`, `.result` and `.failure`; `helena.contracts.v1` is what you import directly. Build a request with `RequestVersions(...)` (eight dimensions plus `model_requested`) and a `Rendering` whose five sections are exactly `SECTIONS`, in that order -- the renderer you are about to write (task 27-29) fills `RenderedSection.body`, `evidence_ids` and `Truncation`, and MUST NOT need to edit `v1.py`, which is frozen. `tests/test_contracts.py` has ready-made builders (`versions()`, `rendering()`, `cost()`, `request()`, `result()`, `failure()`) worth copying rather than re-deriving; note that every model is `strict=True`, so an `int` where a `float` is declared is a validation error and tuples are required where a `tuple[...]` is declared. Call `check_exchange(request, outcome)` from orchestration -- it is the only place the echoed versions, the citation resolution and the truncation-visibility rule are enforced, and no model_post_init can do it. Two things the contract deliberately does not do and that are yours: filtering the rendering to evidence tier `enrichment` for triage (task 28 lists it; the rendering carries no tier), and enforcing the budgets, which concept/07 puts at the tool boundary. When you first store an assessment, the version dimensions are `helena.versions.VERSION_COLUMNS` and the citations are join rows `(assessment, evidence, role)`, not a JSON array. One thing about the tree that is NOT this task's: `git worktree list` shows a second workspace, `.claude/worktrees/marp-prototype-overview-9c9f76` on branch `claude/marp-prototype-overview-9c9f76`, and it was there before this session started (it sits at 08cd835, the commit this task began from). It is Claude Code's own gitignored workspace directory, not an unreleased task branch -- CONTEXT.md §4's precondition is about a `task-*` branch, and there is none. Do not remove it: resolving another session's workspace is the operator's call.
